answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 169 answers need 169 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the pigment index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the nectar audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the quartz identifier and voids the later submissions, as a result the operator pays for 169 runs and collects one. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
